Power the Pacific Northwest: Shape the Future of Clean Energy as our Internal Operations Leader The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is at the heart of the Pacific Northwest's clean energy lifeline, operating one of the nation's largest and most reliable high-voltage transmission grids.

Behind the physical lines and substations that power millions of homes and businesses is a dedicated engine of operational excellence. As the Internal Operations Manager, you will step into a pivotal, high-visibility role as the operational "chief of staff" for our Construction and Maintenance Services division.

You will lead the critical planning, budgeting, and administrative strategies that empower our field crews to execute grid-modernization projects safely, efficiently, and on schedule.

If you are a strategic thinker who thrives at the intersection of team leadership, resource optimization, and high-impact project support, this is your opportunity to drive real-world impact on the future of clean energy.

Key Responsibilities of the Role Here are the eight most impactful and rewarding duties of this position, redesigned to highlight your strategic influence and leadership impact: Serve as a Chief Strategic Advisor Directly partner with senior executive leadership to shape, implement, and evaluate regional grid construction and maintenance programs.

In this trusted advisory role, you will provide critical data, analytical insights, and strategic recommendations that influence high-level decision-making. Lead, Mentor, and Empower a High-Performing Team Provide direct leadership and oversight to a talented team of professional and administrative experts.

You will establish performance standards, foster professional growth, resolve workplace disputes, and champion a collaborative, inclusive culture built on mutual respect and shared success. Drive Multi-Million-Dollar Portfolio and Budget Planning Take ownership of long-range program planning, budgeting, and workload scheduling.

You will oversee resource allocations and monitor third-party contractor portfolios to ensure critical infrastructure projects are executed on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards.

Build and Navigate Key Stakeholder Alliances Represent the agency in critical negotiations and collaborative efforts with executive leaders, federal and state partners, regional public and private utility providers, and manufacturing representatives. You will serve as a key broker in aligning regional interests and securing essential resources.

Champion Process Innovation and Efficiency Identify and eliminate operational bottlenecks. You will foster a forward-thinking, cost-conscious, and results-oriented environment by designing and implementing modern, streamlined workflows that continuously improve operational delivery.

Navigate Regulatory Compliance and Grid Modernization Interpret and apply national energy guidelines and utility performance standards (including NERC and FERC regulations). You will ensure that all planning, construction, and asset-management initiatives align with national compliance frameworks to protect grid reliability.

Shape Long-Term Workforce and Contract Strategies Determine long-range staffing requirements and make high-level decisions on whether to leverage internal personnel or contract work out to private partners. You will design annual and long-range strategic work plans that align administrative resources with field operations.

Champion Safety and Field Readiness Oversee and coordinate critical technical craft and safety training programs across the Pacific Northwest. You will ensure that field personnel are fully equipped, certified, and compliant with safety standards to successfully execute high-risk construction projects.
SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS: A qualified candidate's online application and resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level [GS-12] in the Federal service.

Specialized experience for this position is defined as: 1) Providing program management and analytical advisory services to management in the areas of work planning, scheduling, budgeting, and cost analysis within a utility, construction, production, or maintenance organization; and 2) Performing lead or supervisory duties such as planning and assigning work, establishing performance standards, and resolving administrative or employee grievances.

"Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience. Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Time-in-Grade: Current Federal employees must meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement to receive consideration. CTAP/ICTAP candidates: To be considered "well qualified" you must meet all of the requirements as described in this section.

You must meet all qualifications and eligibility requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

A day in the life: The AI Operations Manager is the operating system behind the Innovation team. You administer the company's enterprise AI platforms, keep the SVP and the team's initiatives moving in sync, keep the roadmap current, and act as an early-warning system for what is changing at the AI frontier.

Early on the work is operations-heavy; your strategic voice is expected to grow as you automate the operations down. You are a force multiplier, not a support function.

Responsibilities: - Administer the company's enterprise AI platforms - Claude Enterprise, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, and new tools as we adopt them - covering provisioning, access, RBAC, usage governance, and billing, and automate that administration down over time. - Keep the SVP of Innovation organized and ahead of schedule through prioritization, prep, and follow-through - you catch what would otherwise slip before it does. - Run the Innovation team's weekly operating rhythm and keep the roadmap current and trusted at all times. - Produce a weekly AI intelligence brief on what is shipping at the frontier and what the team should test. - Bring a point of view into strategy conversations and grow into a genuine strategic voice for the team. - Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department. - Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements: 2-4 years of experience; early-career with an unusually high ceiling and a fast learning rate. AI-native - you use Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini daily and have real intuition for what they can and cannot do. This is the non-negotiable bar. A strong organizer who makes chaos legible and closes loops without being chased.

A clear writer and systems thinker who holds a point of view. Comfortable being the least experienced person in the room and still adding value. Meaningful daily overlap with U.S. Pacific hours (LATAM timezones ideal); remote, open to international candidates. Bonus: you have built something with AI - an agent, a workflow, or a shipped side project.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - Enterprise AI platform access and provisioning requests resolved within one business day, fully documented. - Admin time trending down quarter over quarter as workflows get automated. - Weekly AI intelligence brief shipped on time, every week. - Roadmap accurate and current at any given moment - never a scramble to update it. - Zero missed commitments or dropped follow-ups traceable to coordination gaps.

Most Important Things (MITs) - Be the reason the Innovation team's operations run without friction. - Keep the SVP focused on the highest-leverage work by owning everything beneath it. - Turn AI platform administration into a system that mostly runs itself. - Act as an early-warning system for what is changing in AI - surface it before it is obvious. - Earn a real voice in strategy by being right, useful, and fast.

Field Operations Manager Location Remote (U.S.) with occasional travel to customer sites, TurbineOne facilities, demonstrations, and operational events as required. About TurbineOne TurbineOne is building Mission-AI for the Frontlines.

Our Frontline Perception System (FPS) helps military and national security operators detect threats, accelerate decision-making, and unlock the power of AI at the tactical edge. We endeavor to build mission-valuable products in command and control, autonomy, and AI-enabled mission systems.

We partner directly with frontline users to deliver mission-ready capabilities that work in real-world environments where speed, trust, reliability, and operational resilience matter most. Our team is composed of experienced technologists, veterans, and operators committed to advancing national security through responsible innovation.

The Role The Field Operations Manager owns the operational systems that make Field Engineering deployable, repeatable, and scalable. This is a builder role; you will start as an Individual Contributor (IC) with extended team support, responsible for defining the operational models and discipline.

Over time, you will build and lead a team to perform these functions. You will partner closely with Field Engineering, Mission Operations, Product, Engineering, Security, BD, and leadership to ensure every field engagement has the right people, equipment, information, and operating cadence to succeed. Core Responsibility Areas

Field Engagement Operations: Own the end-to-end operational workflow for Field Engineering from resourcing and readiness to execution and closeout. Maintain the field engagement tracker, validate upcoming requests, and drive pre-deployment planning discipline.

Field Hardware: Own the operational readiness of field hardware. Coordinate imaging, configuration, software versioning, testing, and shipping for deployments and demos. Maintain standard loadouts and coordinate with Engineering/IT/DevOps.

Field Asset Management: Create and maintain the asset-management system. Track inventory, custody, location, status, and lifecycle management for all field gear.

Field Knowledge Management: Own the field knowledge base. Maintain SOPs, checklists, templates, and AARs. Ensure lessons learned are captured and reusable.

Field Communications: Own communication rhythms. Translate product updates into field-relevant guidance, coordinate daily SITREPs, and provide operational updates to leadership.

Field Enablement: Own the Field Engineering readiness model. Build onboarding pathways, define readiness requirements, and run enablement sessions and assessments to ensure FEs are prepared for mission types and hardware loadouts.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
4+ years of experience in Field Operations, Technical Enablement, Customer Success, or Systems Engineering, with a specific focus on building and scaling operational systems.
2+ years of experience leading or managing teams (this role transitions from a hands-on IC builder to a team lead).
Proven track record of operationalizing informal or ad-hoc processes into repeatable, scalable operating models.
Strong proficiency in scripting languages (e.g., Python, Bash) for automation, data routing, and operational tooling.
Experience supporting production software deployed into mission-critical, disconnected, or hybrid environments.

U.S. Citizenship. Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Security Clearance.

Experience supporting Department of Defense or Intelligence Community software programs, including accreditation activities (RMF, ATO, IATT).
Experience with Field Enablement and Field Resource Management.
Experience deploying and managing software/hardware at the tactical edge.
Background in both technical engineering and operational management (dual-hat experience is highly valued).
Familiarity with AI/ML platforms and mission software ecosystems.
What Success Looks Like
The Field Engineering team consistently executes against clearly defined priorities with high reliability across all customer sites.
Customer deployments occur smoothly with minimal operational disruption.
Field Engineering tools and processes mature over time to support the growth of the company.
Field tooling and standardized workflows significantly reduce time-to-deployment and increase on-site success rates..
Field Engineering is viewed as a strategic enabler that bridges the gap between core engineering and tactical mission success.
Team members grow professionally while contributing to a culture of continuous improvement.

You'll join a team of experienced technologists, veterans, and mission-focused professionals committed to solving some of the nation's most challenging operational problems through responsible innovation.

About Maneva Maneva is an AI services company founded by a former Google DeepMind researcher, focused on transforming manufacturing operations through advanced AI. We enable autonomous factory operation and optimization by generating AI-driven actions and insights using off-the-shelf hardware or existing vision systems.

We've grown rapidly and are well-funded, technically exceptional, and mission-driven. As we grow, we're building a people-first culture that attracts, develops, and retains world-class talent. Role Overview Maneva is seeking a People & Business Operations Manager to build and lead our people operations function at a critical stage of growth.

This role sits at the intersection of employee lifecycle management, governance, business operations, and culture.

You'll own performance management infrastructure, compensation and benefits administration, employee relations, U.S. state-level employment compliance as we expand our U.S. footprint, and will help drive the initiatives of the strategy and business operations team.

You'll be responsible for building the systems that let us hire, develop, and retain great people as we continue our fast expansion. You'll work closely with the Talent Manager, Finance, Business Operations, and the broader executive leadership team, and act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and leadership team on people matters.

Key Responsibilities U.S. Employment Compliance Own state-by-state compliance as Maneva expands its U.S. employee base: tax registration, payroll setup, mandatory workplace posters, and required employee notices, all of which vary by state.

Build and maintain a repeatable process for evaluating new-state requirements as hiring expands, rather than handling each state reactively. Partner with Rippling, outside counsel, and Finance to ensure payroll, tax, and notice obligations are met on schedule for every state in which Maneva has employees.

Serve as Maneva 's go-to internal expert on U.S. state employment law as it applies to a distributed, remote-first workforce. Performance Management & Levelling Design and execute performance review cycles (6-month and annual) across the organization, tailored to company growth stage and business needs.

Own and maintain levelling frameworks across engineering (IC1–IC6) and non-technical roles; define competencies, expectations, and progression criteria, building on the framework already in place. Partner with department heads and the Talent Manager to calibrate performance data and inform talent decisions.

Design and facilitate manager training on feedback, goal-setting, and performance conversations. Maintain performance documentation and analytics to inform strategic people decisions. Compensation Administration Own day-to-day execution of compensation administration across all job levels and geographies; maintain salary bands.

Execute variable/commission plans for sales and other roles; ensure alignment with business goals. More About the Opportunity
Merchandising at Grove runs on real expertise and too much manual glue.
Buyers chase vendors for the same data, week after week.
Marketing launches promotions inventory finds out about too late.
Good people spend their time on work a workflow should be doing for them.
We have an internal AI team. They coach. They don't build for you.
This role is for the person who wants their hands on the keyboard, not the person who scopes it and waits.

Some of what you build will work on the first try. Some won't. That's the job.

Map how merchandising actually works today, not how the org chart says it works.
Redesign core operating processes for speed, accuracy, and margin protection: assortment planning, item setup, pricing and markdown, vendor and PO management, allocation, replenishment.

Build the automation yourself, using Claude and comparable AI tools, no/low-code platforms, and lightweight automation, from concept through rollout.
Run pilots end to end: scope, build, test for accuracy, validate fit, scale. Keep humans in the loop on margin- and inventory-critical decisions.
Maintain a registry of approved tools and active automations, so what exists and what it's for is never a mystery.
Own change management for every rollout: training, AI literacy for non-technical audiences, office hours, a bench of power users.
Build reporting on process and automation performance, and use it to prioritize what gets built next.
